blurb: Large white Italian flock guardian used for centuries to protect sheep from wolves
description: The Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog is a large livestock guardian from central Italy, with a thick, rough solid-white coat and a calm, protective nature.
answer: The Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog is a large Italian livestock guardian dog from central Italy, especially the Maremma and Abruzzo, used for centuries to protect sheep from wolves. It stands roughly 62 to 74 cm tall, weighs about 35 to 52 kg, and has a thick, rough white coat.

body: White flock guardian dogs are described in ancient Roman writings by Columella, Varro and Palladius, and similar dogs appear in Italian art from Roman times onward. The name combines the Maremma marshlands, where flocks over-wintered, and Abruzzo, where sheep herding and the Apennine wolf remain part of rural life. The dogs played a central role in the transhumance, the annual movement of flocks between mountain and lowland pastures.

The first four dogs were registered in Italy in 1898 and the first standard was drawn up in 1924. The Maremmano and the Abruzzese were treated as separate breeds until 1958, when the Italian kennel club unified them, citing a natural fusion of the two types.

The breed has a solid, muscular build, a large head and a black nose, lips and eye rims. The coat is long, thick and rough to the touch, forming a heavy collar around the neck. It should be solid white, though slight yellowing may be tolerated. Some dogs are considerably larger than the typical range.

As a working guardian, the breed is traditionally described as protecting by dissuasion rather than fighting; physical combat with predators is relatively rare. Working dogs operate in groups of three or four and are raised among sheep from before 40 days old with minimal human contact so they bond with the flock.

Sources focus on the breed's working role rather than home care. Its dense coat and guardian background suggest it is suited to outdoor life with livestock; it has been used to guard sheep, cattle and even little penguins on Middle Island in Australia.

The median age at death has been reported as 7.5 years, compared with a median of 10 years for all dogs in Italy. The source text does not name specific conditions; breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: What is the Maremma Sheepdog used for?
faq.a: It is a livestock guardian traditionally used to protect sheep from wolves, and it has also guarded cattle, and penguins from foxes in Australia.

faq.q: How big does a Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog get?
faq.a: It is a large dog, roughly 62 to 74 cm at the shoulder and about 35 to 52 kg, with some dogs considerably larger.

faq.q: Is the Maremmano-Abruzzese Sheepdog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 201 in Group 1, with Italy as the country of origin.
